promptLatex: In triangle $ABC$, $m\angle A = 50^{\circ}$ and $m\angle B = 60^{\circ}$. An exterior angle of the triangle is drawn at vertex $C$. What is its measure, in degrees?
hintLatex: An exterior angle is measured along a straight line, so it and the interior angle at that vertex fill $180^{\circ}$.
There is also a direct reading: the exterior angle collects the two angles at the other vertices.
Adding the two remote interior angles gives $50^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}$.
solutionLatex:
The exterior angle at $C$ forms a linear pair with $m\angle C$, and the angle sum gives $m\angle C = 180^{\circ} - 50^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}$.

So the exterior angle is $180^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}$.

The same value comes from the exterior angle theorem, which says the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $50^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}$.
